subject: Japanese white-eye
title: Birds Swallowed These Snails Whole. 1 in 7 Came Out Alive

scenes.text: A bird swallows a snail whole. Half an hour later, the snail crawls away.
On Japan's Ogasawara Islands, scientists fed one hundred seventy-four tiny land snails to birds.
Each snail was only two and a half millimetres, smaller than a grain of rice.
The trip through the bird's gut took thirty to forty minutes. About fifteen percent came out alive.
One survivor even gave birth soon after it came out.
Why it matters: a bird flies off before it poops. Getting eaten may be how these snails travel.

description:
In a 2011 Tohoku University study, tiny 2.5 mm land snails (Tornatellides boeningi) fed to Japanese white-eyes and brown-eared bulbuls passed through in 30 to 40 minutes, and about 15% survived.
One snail gave birth soon after; genetic data suggest birds may spread the snails between sites.
Would you have believed a snail could survive being eaten?
first_comment: 14% survived white-eyes and 16% survived bulbuls. What's the strangest way you've heard of an animal getting around?
